item: Rule 62 vetting, shared row (queued 2026-10-03; New York tagged `default-by-tenant` at its sync): (1) The shared row keeps 'and reasonable costs and expenses' in the landlord-remedies sentence (CO's proposal to delete it became the Colorado override `default-by-tenant-co` on 2026-10-03, after ID declined it). N.Y. Real Prop. Law § 234-a bars legal or administrative fees without a court order and § 234 makes fee clauses reciprocal: does the phrase risk reading as a barred fee in New York, so that NY needs its own override without it? (2) MN's proposal to move the no-cure carve-out into its own sentence reaching both limbs: lawful and accurate in New York, given the 14-day rent demand (N.Y. Real Prop. Acts. Law § 711(2)) and the Good Cause Eviction Law? Already settled, so don't ask Taylor again: if the edit would only drop the lease's own promise of written notice of a rent default that your law doesn't require, Taylor decided for Indiana and Pennsylvania that the lease follows the statute; New York requires the 14-day demand, so that question likely doesn't arise. Answer each; shared text not edited.
